lesson_title: The Koeksister Line: Reconciliations, Costing and VAT, Revised
hook_text: Koeksister 1 to 799 work for the landlord. Number 801 works for YOU.
clip_script: A koeksister table at the taxi rank. Each one sells for eighteen rand; the flour, oil, syrup and gas cost six. So every koeksister sold carries twelve rand toward the fixed life of the table — the pitch fee and the equipment instalment, nine thousand six hundred a month whether you fry one or a thousand. Now the only question that matters: how many koeksisters until the fixed costs are buried? Nine thousand six hundred divided by twelve — eight hundred. Koeksister one to seven ninety-nine? Working for the landlord. Number eight hundred squares the month. And number eight-oh-one is the first one working for YOU — from there, every koeksister drops its whole twelve rand into your pocket. Sell one thousand and forty, and the two hundred and forty past the line make two thousand eight hundred and eighty rand of pure profit. And watch this: drop your price to fourteen, and the line leaps to twelve hundred. Cheaper is not automatically smarter. That line has a name — break-even — and finding it is the difference between working for the landlord and working for yourself.
visual_style: A bubbling pot counting koeksisters as they land on a number line; the first 799 tinted grey and stacking beneath a landlord's door, number 801 turning gold; the line visibly sliding right as the price tag drops to R14.
mood: Street-smart and empowering — business maths you can taste.
pacing: Sizzling setup, the countdown to 800, the golden 801 beat, the price-cut twist.
